newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH 1-DAY RATES SEEN UP AFTER MONTH-END TUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH 1-DAY RATES SEEN UP AFTER MONTH-END TUMBLE.

text.p: Polish one-day rates are expected to rise to above 21 percent on Friday after surplus cash at the end of the financial month on Thursday sent rates tumbling.

"After today's crash one-day rates should return to above 21 percent on Friday and continue to hold around there next week, when obligatory reserves are higher," said Piotr Schmidt, deposits dealer at Pekao SA.

Last month the central bank said that from February 28 it was increasing mandatory reserves on zloty call deposits to 20 percent from the current 17 percent and was doubling the reserves on currency deposits to four percent.
Dealers said the reserves increase would not significantly increase market deposit rates unless the central bank also pushed up its reverse repo rates, now around 21.60 percent.

Overnight rates closed at 7.00/9.50 percent on Thursday, down from opening's 8.00/13.00 percent as banks found funds after squaring required reserve accounts. Tomorrow/next were at 21.55/21.85 percent, up from Wednesday's 19.50/21.30.
The Polish zloty closed a fraction weaker on Thursday after drifting without direction for most of the day, dealers said.
It was at 2.91/2.82 percent from the trading band centre, down from yesterday's 2.96/2.89 percent.
The zloty was at 3.0565/85 to the dollar, down from 3.0395/10 on Wednesday and at 1.8080/00 to the mark, up from 1.8150/70. It was fixed flat at 2.88 percent from parity.
